title: Staying compliant: returns, honest labels and records

say: Staying compliant: annual returns, honest labels, and records.
This is the video for module three of Business Registration and Compliance in Nigeria.
Registration is a one-time event. Compliance is a habit. An annual return tells the CAC, once a year: we are still here, and this is who we are. It is not the same as a tax return.

say: Packaged food, drinks, cosmetics and chemicals need NAFDAC registration. Other manufactured goods may need SON. A service only needs CAC and tax.
For example, Ifeyinwa in Owerri sells pepper sauce with a sticker that says NAFDAC approved and boosts immunity. She has not applied to NAFDAC yet.

panel.heading: Fixing a label before NAFDAC
right: Space for NAFDAC number and batch

say: She removes NAFDAC approved at once, and the health claim she cannot prove. She adds ingredients, the net content, her business name and address, and space for the NAFDAC number, batch and dates.
Never print a number you have not been given. Products with false claims can be seized.

panel.heading: Fixing a label before NAFDAC

say: The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 protects names, phone numbers and payment details. Collect only what you need, tell customers why, and never share their details without consent.

cards.d: Collect only what you need, say why, no broadcast lists without agreement.
Record the batch number, stop selling that batch, respond respectfully.
Your name, your login, your signature on the account. Write co-owner shares down.

say: If a customer reports a problem with a food or cosmetic, record the batch number and stop selling that batch until you understand it.

say: Keep four records: sales, expenses, receipts and bank statements. A notebook or free phone spreadsheet is enough, if you use it every day. Here is what that gives you.

say: Nigeria's new tax laws took effect on 1 January 2026, so guidance is still developing. A company files company income tax returns with the Nigeria Revenue Service.

panel.heading: Zero tax is not zero filing
items: Company: files with the NRS
Small company: 0 percent tax, still files
Business name: personal tax via your state
Keep records for six years

say: A company that meets the legal definition of a small company pays 0 percent company income tax, but it must still file.

panel.heading: Zero tax is not zero filing

Business name: personal tax via your state
Keep records for six years

say: A business name owner pays personal income tax on profit through her State Internal Revenue Service.

say: Companies must keep accounting records for six years. Even when tax due is nothing, filing proves you are compliant and helps you get a tax clearance certificate.

say: To remember. File your annual return every year, and report changes promptly. Keep labels honest. Keep four simple records and back them up. And even when tax is zero, file.

panel.heading: Remember
items: File your annual return every year
Report changes on the portal promptly
Never show a NAFDAC number you do not have
Keep sales, expenses, receipts, statements
Zero tax still means filing
